newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: REFITTING OF S.AFRICAN ORIBI OIL RIG DELAYED.
newsitem.headline: REFITTING OF S.AFRICAN ORIBI OIL RIG DELAYED.

text.p: The refitting of the oil rig destined to start pumping South Africa's first oil field has been delayed but first oil output is still expected in February.

The rig is to drill in the Oribi field 140 km southwest of Mossel Bay. State-owned oil exploration company Soekor and its 20 percent partner, Energy Africa Ltd , plan to pump the oil into a one million barrel shuttle tanker for shipment to one of South Africa's three coastal refineries.
The $75 million project is being funded by syndicated loans and Soekor is confident that capital costs will be recovered within the first year of operation.

Site manager Jon Hawkes told Reuters on Friday that the original mid-November target for the completion of work on the ORCA rig in Simon's Town harbour had not been met because of slow progress due to bad weather.
"The target date is now to leave the harbour at the end of November and after that there will still be a further week of loading and then a further week of sea trials after that."
Production was scheduled for the beginning of February but was now likely to be the end of February, Hawkes said.
Development of the oil field will be a done by Schlumberger Logelco Inc and Fred Olsen Production of Norway to develop the oil field and they would source people internationally and locally.
With an expected production rate of 20,000 barrels of oil a day, the new field will be small by world standards but will supply six percent of South Africa's current crude oil needs.
